Playbook.name: Linux — Linux init (PID 1) Secret Dump via GDB - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Credential Access — OS Credential Dumping (Proc Filesystem)

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A debugger (gdb) was used to attach to PID 1 (init/systemd) — the classic "gdb --pid 1" / "gdb -p 1" technique that walks the memory of the longest-lived, most-privileged process to carve out secrets (environment variables, credentials, tokens) from /proc/1/mem. The triage question: is this a developer/administrator debugging init, or an attacker harvesting secrets from process memory? CRITICAL JCB DETECTION CONSTRAINT (verified live): the shipped detection rule is EQL keyed on process start/exec (event.type=="start", event.action in ("exec","exec_event"), process.name=="gdb"), but JCB Linux auditd does NOT audit execve — auditd_manager emits no exec/executed events — so THE RULE AS WRITTEN CANNOT FIRE HERE. The only telemetry that captures a gdb invocation is auditd USER_CMD (logs-auditd.log-*), which records sudo-invoked commands with their arguments. This playbook is built on that real telemetry.
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: PID 1 runs as root and holds long-lived secrets in memory; dumping it can expose service credentials, tokens and keys that unlock lateral movement across the banking estate. Because the process is init, the technique is stealthy and rarely part of normal operations.

Assets.AssetType: Linux servers (core banking, application, database — INTDOM)

LogSources.LogSource: Linux auditd USER_CMD records — logs-auditd.log-* (verified live: sudo commands with process.args + auditd.log.AUID — the actor-bearing telemetry)
Elastic auditd_manager — logs-auditd_manager.auditd-* (verified live: session/login/ran-command with user.name — session context only, NO command args, NO execve)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: auditd shipping to logs-auditd.log-* with USER_CMD records carrying process.args and auditd.log.AUID (verified live).

NO EXECVE AUDITING: JCB auditd does not audit execve or file syscalls (verified — auditd_manager has zero exec/executed actions). The EQL rule that defines this detection cannot fire; treat any case as originating from a promotion/manual hunt and pivot immediately to USER_CMD.

PARTIAL COVERAGE: USER_CMD captures only sudo-invoked gdb. A gdb run while already root, or by a non-sudo process, has no record. Full coverage needs auditd execve auditing or Elastic Defend / MDE-for-Linux device telemetry.

Signal.Name: gdb attached to PID 1
Signal.Details: A USER_CMD whose arguments contain gdb together with a PID-1 target (--pid 1 / -p 1 / attach 1) or a /proc/1/ reference. auditd.log.AUID names the invoking user.

Signal.Name: Anomalous debugger use
Signal.Details: gdb is not part of routine banking-server operations; its appearance via sudo against init is inherently notable.

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Linux host where gdb was invoked (host.name from the alert / hunt).

ImmediateCapture.Item: Invoking user (auditd.log.AUID) and the exact gdb command line, from INV-01
Whether the case arose from a manual hunt / promotion (expected, since the EQL rule cannot fire natively)

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance — the debugger-against-init behaviour is rare, so a confirmed gdb-vs-PID-1 by a non-developer AUID is high-suspicion even without other signals.
No USER_CMD hit does NOT clear the alert: the invocation may have been run as root or non-sudo, outside auditd coverage — inspect the host in that case.

Investigation.Goal: Decide whether gdb attaching to PID 1 on $hostname is legitimate debugging or attacker credential access from process memory, using auditd USER_CMD for the command/actor and auditd_manager for session context.

Step.name: Confirm the gdb-vs-PID-1 invocation (auditd USER_CMD)
Step.Purpose: Establish the anchor fact: was gdb actually pointed at PID 1, by whom, and when. USER_CMD is the only JCB telemetry carrying the command arguments and the invoking user.
Step.Query: FROM logs-auditd.log-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND auditd.log.record_type == "USER_CMD" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cmd = MV_CONCAT(process.args, " ") | WHERE cmd LIKE "*gdb*" AND (cmd RLIKE ".*(--pid|-p)( |=)?1( |$).*" OR cmd RLIKE ".*attach +1( |$).*" OR cmd LIKE "*/proc/1/*") | KEEP @timestamp, auditd.log.AUID, auditd.log.UID, process.executable, cmd, host.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A hit confirms the technique and names the AUID. A developer debugging on a non-production host may be benign; the same command on a production banking server by a non-developer AUID is credential access. If this returns nothing but the case was raised, the invocation likely ran as root/non-sudo — go straight to on-host inspection (INV-02/03 give surrounding context).

Step.name: Profile the invoking user's sudo activity
Step.Purpose: Separate an admin/developer doing maintenance from an attacker escalating: the invoking AUID's other sudo commands in the window tell that story.
Step.Query: FROM logs-auditd.log-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND auditd.log.record_type == "USER_CMD" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cmd = MV_CONCAT(process.args, " ") | STATS commands = COUNT(*), sample_cmds = VALUES(cmd), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY auditd.log.AUID | SORT commands DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A known admin AUID running package/service maintenance around the gdb command is consistent with legitimate debugging. An AUID whose other commands include credential access, memory reading (dd on /proc, strings), enumeration or tunnelling around the gdb use points to an attacker. AUID is the real login user even under su/sudo.

Step.name: Session context on the host (auditd_manager)
Step.Purpose: Corroborate who was logged in / active on $hostname around the event — auditd_manager carries user.name on sessions and ran-command even though it lacks command arguments.
Step.Query: FROM logs-auditd_manager.auditd-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND event.action IN ("logged-in","ran-command","started-session","was-authorized") | STATS n = COUNT(*), users = VALUES(user.name), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY event.action | SORT n DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A single expected admin session aligns with legitimate work. An unfamiliar user, an interactive session from an unusual source, or a burst of ran-command around the gdb invocation strengthens the attacker hypothesis. This step does not carry command text — treat it as corroboration for the AUID identified in INV-01/INV-02.

Node.Condition: INV-01 confirms gdb attached to PID 1 (or /proc/1/mem) by an AUID that is not a developer/administrator, and INV-02 shows surrounding credential-access / enumeration / tunnelling activity.
Node.Result: True Positive (Credential Access — secret dump from init memory — escalate to IR)

Node.Condition: INV-01 confirms the technique on a production banking host and the invoking AUID cannot be tied to an approved debugging/maintenance task.
Node.Result: True Positive (Unauthorised debugger against init — escalate to IR)

Node.Condition: INV-01 names a known developer/admin AUID, INV-02 shows legitimate troubleshooting (service crash, core-dump analysis) and INV-03 shows an expected session, on a host where such debugging is sanctioned.
A monitoring/diagnostic tool or automation account attaches a debugger to init as part of a known (if ill-advised) job whose scope matches the activity.
Node.Result: Misconfiguration (Diagnostic automation touching PID 1 — fix the job; review its rights)

Node.Condition: The case was raised but INV-01 returns no USER_CMD (invocation as root/non-sudo, outside auditd coverage) and intent cannot be established remotely.
Node.Result: Needs Escalation (inspect the host directly — coverage gap)

FalsePositive.Definition: A developer or administrator legitimately debugged init/systemd (crash analysis, diagnostics) on a host where that is sanctioned — the authorising context must be shown, not assumed from "it's an admin".

Indicators.Item: INV-01 AUID is a known developer/SRE with an approved troubleshooting task or ticket.
INV-02 shows only related diagnostic commands, no credential access or lateral-movement tooling.
Host is a non-production / sanctioned-debugging environment.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the debugging task and the operator's authorisation; close as false_positive.
If a specific diagnostic workflow recurs, scope an exception to that AUID/host — do not disable the analytic.

TruePositive.Definition: An adversary attached a debugger to PID 1 to read init's memory and harvest long-lived root-held secrets (environment variables, credentials, tokens) for reuse and lateral movement.

Indicators.Item: gdb-vs-PID-1 confirmed (INV-01) by an unexpected/unauthorised AUID.
Surrounding credential-access, enumeration or egress activity in INV-02/INV-03.
Production banking host; no debugging change record.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the host; preserve auditd/session evidence and any dump artefacts left on disk.
Treat every secret reachable from init's environment as exposed — rotate service credentials/tokens; hunt for their reuse across the estate.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An internal monitoring/diagnostic tool or automation attaches a debugger to init as part of a known job — operationally driven, not malicious, but over-privileged.

Indicators.Item: A service/automation AUID performs the attach on a schedule.
Behaviour matches a documented diagnostic job that should not be touching PID 1.

SOCAction.Item: Engage the tool owner to remove or constrain the debugger step; reduce the account's rights.
Track under configuration hygiene; do not blanket-exception the rule.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: From INV-01 confirm the gdb-vs-PID-1 command and the AUID; from INV-02/INV-03 assess whether the surrounding activity is diagnostic or adversarial.
If the AUID is unauthorised or unattributable on a production host, isolate $hostname and preserve volatile evidence before the operator can clean up.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Reconstruct the invoking user's full session on-host; identify any dumped file / piped output and what was extracted.
Rotate all secrets reachable from init's memory (service accounts, tokens, keys); hunt for their reuse; contain the source identity.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enable auditd execve auditing (or Elastic Defend / MDE-for-Linux device telemetry) so this technique is captured natively and the EQL detection can actually fire.
Restrict who may run debuggers on production hosts; consider ptrace_scope hardening (kernel.yama.ptrace_scope) to block cross-process attach.

Escalation.Trigger: Confirmed gdb-vs-PID-1 by an unauthorised/unattributable AUID, any occurrence on a production banking host, or surrounding credential-access activity.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Invoking AUID and debugging task confirmed authorised on a sanctioned host, with a matching ticket.
No credential-access or lateral-movement activity surrounding the invocation.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host isolated and inspected; dump artefacts identified; exposed secrets rotated.
Source identity contained; reuse swept across the estate; incident documented and the execve-auditing coverage gap recorded for remediation.
